title: SAT Nonlinear Functions & Graphs: Read Any Graph, Table, or Shift
description:
SAT function questions show up as equations, graphs, tables, and word problems, but they all test the same idea: inputs and outputs. This lesson covers the official SAT skill "nonlinear functions" from the ground up, with 6 SAT-style practice questions that get harder as they go.

You'll learn:
• Function notation: f(a), f(x) = k, and compositions like g(f(4))
• How to read intercepts, maximums and minimums, and solution counts from a graph
• Why f(x − 2) shifts a graph RIGHT, and what −f(x) does
• What the numbers mean in quadratic and exponential models
• When to use Desmos (and when not to bother)

All questions are original SAT-style questions written for this video, not official College Board questions. For official practice, use the free SAT Suite Question Bank (Advanced Math → Nonlinear functions).
